doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Own sound and the film Bird
title: Blues over Stravinsky's Firebird and Hollywood click tracks
summary: Eastwood had him play a Kansas City blues over the Firebird Suite in the Stravinsky scene; he describes click-track scoring.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Was there any attempt to figure out, well, what key is his piece in?

Well it didn’t make any difference. In fact, the fact that it was happening, it was just super — it was like Charles Ives, it was just superimposed, it didn’t make any difference. And in fact it worked really well, it was very, very interesting.
So it was interesting how that Hollywood click track stuff works and just the technology and how they write music for scenes, you know I’d never done that before.
